title: Who We Serve: Contractors, Fleets, Energy, CPOs | Anari
meta: Four customer types we serve in emerging EV markets: engineering contractors, fleet operators, energy and real estate firms, independent CPO entrepreneurs.

sections.h1: You bring the site, the fleet, the capital or the plan.
sections.lede: Four starting points, one destination: a charging business you own and operate. The delivery scope is the same; what changes is which asset you already have and what you are missing.
sections.credit: Corridor deployment · dual-gun 120 kW, Central Asia

sections.lede: Shares above are the demand mix across our turnkey program in emerging markets — not a ranking of who matters more.

items.title: Engineering contractors
items.text: You build the site and can deliver the works — you need a charging product line, permits and an operations layer.

items.title: Fleet operators
items.text: You control the vehicles and the yard — you need the charging design that survives your worst operating night.

items.title: Energy & real estate
items.text: You own the land, the power or the tenants — you need the commercial model that makes the site worth building.

items.title: Independent CPO entrepreneurs
items.text: You have the plan and the market — you need everything between a site decision and a running business.

sections.h2: The gap is different, the scope is not
sections.lede: All seven workstreams stay in scope. What shifts is where the project is most likely to fail first — and therefore which stage gets the most attention.

items.title: Contractors
items.text: Strengths: civil and electrical works. Usual gap: product specification, compliance paperwork and post-handover operations.

items.title: Fleets
items.text: Strengths: the vehicles and the operating pattern. Usual gap: grid capacity for the peak duty cycle, and the migration path when the fleet changes.

items.title: Energy & real estate
items.text: Strengths: land, power and tenants. Usual gap: utilisation assumptions and the commercial model, which decide whether the site ever pays back.

items.title: CPO entrepreneurs
items.text: Strengths: market insight and local relationships. Usual gap: every technical stage at once — which is why the turnkey scope exists.

sections.h2: Tell us which of the four you are, and what you already have.
sections.lede: The fastest useful conversation starts with the asset you control: site, fleet, capital or plan.
